data.name: Diagnosis_CredentialExpired
data.value:
This computer's device credentials are no longer valid, or the device was revoked on the computer.
Generate a new QR code and pair again.
data.comment: Hint for an expired/revoked device credential

data.name: Diagnosis_ProtocolMismatch
data.value:
The client and the computer use different protocol versions, so pairing cannot complete.
Update the Windows client to the latest version (Settings → Check for updates) and make sure the DSH Mobile plugin on the computer is also updated to a compatible version.
data.comment: Hint for a protocol/version mismatch

data.name: Diagnosis_CaMismatch
data.value: The computer connected to is not the one pinned at pairing (CA fingerprint mismatch). Make sure the pairing link comes from this computer and that no address hijacking occurs in between.
data.comment: Hint for a pinned-CA mismatch

data.name: Diagnosis_CpolarStale
data.value:
The temporary cpolar address is no longer valid.
A free cpolar tunnel changes its domain on every restart, so the saved address can no longer reach this computer. Open remote access in DSH Mobile on the computer, copy the new pairing link and paste it again.
data.comment: Hint for a rotated cpolar tunnel address

data.name: Diagnosis_HostUnresolved
data.comment: Hint when the name cannot be resolved (second argument is the LAN/remote advice)

data.name: Diagnosis_HostUnresolvedLan
data.value: Local network connection: make sure this PC and the computer are on the same network and that the gateway is running on the computer.
data.comment: LAN advice for an unresolved name

data.name: Diagnosis_HostUnresolvedRemote
data.value: Remote connection: make sure the remote channel (Tailscale/cpolar/cloudflared etc.) is running and that the domain is reachable.
data.comment: Remote advice for an unresolved name

data.name: Diagnosis_Http426
data.value:
The computer requires a client upgrade to continue (HTTP 426).
Update the Windows client to the latest version (Settings → Check for updates).
data.comment: Hint for HTTP 426

data.name: Diagnosis_Http429
data.value:
The computer is currently limiting new connection requests (HTTP 429).
Wait a minute or two and try again. If this happens often, check whether several clients are reconnecting to the computer at the same time.
data.comment: Hint for HTTP 429

data.name: Diagnosis_ServiceUnavailable
data.value:
The DSH service on the computer is temporarily unavailable (HTTP {0}).
Make sure both the gateway and DSH itself are running on the computer, then retry.
data.comment: Hint for a 5xx answer

data.name: Diagnosis_TlsFailure
data.value:
Failed to establish a secure (TLS) connection to the computer.
Common causes: the computer's certificate changed, a proxy or VPN is intercepting TLS, or the system clock is far off. Make sure the gateway is running on the computer and paste that computer's current pairing link again.
data.comment: Hint for a TLS handshake failure

data.name: Diagnosis_NetworkFailure
data.value:
Cannot establish an HTTPS connection to the gateway on the computer.
{0}
data.comment: Hint when the gateway is unreachable (argument is the LAN/remote advice)

data.name: Diagnosis_NetworkLan
data.value: Local network connection: make sure this PC and the computer are on the same network, the firewall allows the gateway port and the channel is ready.
data.comment: LAN advice for an unreachable gateway

data.name: Diagnosis_NetworkRemote
data.value: Remote connection: make sure the remote channel is running and that the address is reachable from the internet.
data.comment: Remote advice for an unreachable gateway

data.name: Diagnosis_Timeout
data.value: Connection timed out. Make sure the iroh channel on the computer is ready and that both sides are reachable, then retry.
data.comment: Hint for a timeout/cancellation

data.name: Diagnosis_IrohNoAddress
data.comment: iroh discovery found no addressing information

data.name: Diagnosis_IrohConnectTimeout
data.value:
iroh could not reach the computer the pairing points to within 15 seconds (retried automatically twice).
EndpointId: {0} Common causes: the channel on the computer just restarted, the discovery record has not propagated yet, or a proxy/VPN is blocking UDP. Make sure the channel is ready and retry; for details see data\client.log.
data.comment: iroh could not reach the paired endpoint in time

data.name: Diagnosis_CaFetchFailed
data.value: Failed to fetch the pairing CA: {0}
data.comment: GatewayAuth: ca.cer returned a rejection the trust policy will not accept

data.name: Diagnosis_CaResponseEmpty
data.comment: GatewayAuth: empty ca.cer body

data.value: The pairing CA does not match the QR code fingerprint; the computer connected to may not be the one the QR code points to
data.comment: GatewayAuth: fetched CA does not match the pairing fingerprint

data.name: Diagnosis_NoTrustAnchor
data.value: No trust anchor: the pairing CA is missing and platform trust is not allowed
data.comment: GatewayAuth: no trust anchor for the connection

data.name: AppData_UnwritableMessage
data.value:
The program folder is not writable, so settings, paired computers and logs cannot be saved.
Move the whole program folder to a writable location (for example Desktop, Documents or a USB drive) and run it again; do not place it in Program Files or another location that needs administrator rights.
This run can still connect to computers, but no settings are kept after it exits.
